title: Honest Connected Intervals for KL-Balanced Causal Targets at a Moment-Feasibility Boundary
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the delivered result incremental below the field floor: paper_score_ceiling 5.8 < 7.4, with no bounded within-scope repair.
gap_reasons: The note proves an exact local asymptotic minimax characterization only as an implicit Gaussian kernel game and a convergent certification scheme; it does not deliver the requested certified numerical value or establish that connected non-affine intervals improve on the best affine interval.
The sole strict performance result is the affine-over-unrestricted-Wald inequality, while the empirically motivating 3.920-versus-3.951 comparison remains explicitly uncertified.

The attaining causal interval is an existential diagonal construction for a bespoke known sixteen-cell model, not an implemented finite program or a learned-nuisance procedure usable in the named 401(k) application.

Several load-bearing passages—especially arbitrary-procedure transfer for unbounded interval actions and closure of the continuum primal–dual approximation—are argued at theorem-sketch level rather than through a precise cited transfer or duality theorem, further limiting the paper score.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the sixteen-cell causal reduction, a compact Gaussian interval game, a convergent finite-program scheme, and an analytic affine improvement over unrestricted Wald intervals. The proposed stronger connected-versus-affine result was left open after its numerical witness lacked a replayable checker and contained an incorrect affine leaf. The reviewer graded the delivered work incremental below the field floor; a certified continuum bracket, fully rigorous all-procedure transfer, and an observable broader-scope interval remain unresolved.
tldr: In the fully positive binary benchmark, the KL-balanced causal target has a continuous boundary closure although its finite exponential-tilt representation fails at the face, and the exact sign margin identifies when bounded-multiplier regularity is retained. The local problem is an unrestricted Gaussian location plus a bounded one-sided nuisance mean. Its all-connected-interval value is characterized by a no-gap continuum dual, and the finite-cell causal transfer supplies a data-only attaining sequence even on empirical non-straddling samples. Analytically, for every \(\sigma>0\), finite \(H\ge0\), \(0<\alpha<1\), and \(a\ne0\), the connected optimum is no larger than the optimized bias-aware affine length, which is strictly smaller than unrestricted Wald. Whether the connected optimum is strictly smaller than the affine benchmark at the stated \(H=1\) corner remains open pending a replayable rational certificate.
gap: Ghosh--Rothenh\"ausler give regular inference under a finite KL tilt and describe empirical infeasibility, while the expected-size literature gives unrestricted-set duality or finite approximations. None determines the connected-interval value at a one-sided moment-feasibility face, certifies its continuum computation, and transfers it to arbitrary honest causal intervals.
fill: The binary likelihood is reduced to its complete Gaussian boundary experiment; the connected endpoint game is solved by a retained-connectivity dual and certified discretization; the value is lifted to a full effect-box minimax equality with a data-only attaining interval and a strict non-affine benchmark at \(H=1\).
